blocks.explanation: The humanities recast as the retroactive data sciences of the human manifold. History is the macro-thermodynamic ledger — the trajectory of the collective manifold through configuration space, documenting how societies pump negative entropy through agriculture, trade and law to hold their macro-Markov blanket against the environment, and reading wars, famines and collapses as runaway entropic cascades in which the institutional metric tensor can no longer compress environmental complexity and predictive error spikes. Anthropology studies the structural geometry instead: human groups settle into different attractor basins depending on environmental input, with kinship structures, taboos and rituals as local metric tensors regulating multi-agent interaction, and ritual functioning as a synchronization algorithm resetting a group's predictive models to a shared baseline. Philology tracks the temporal derivative of the syntactic metric tensor — language expanding its dimensionality as civilizations meet new complexity, and etymology tracing a concept's geodesic backward, with phonemic shifts read as localized topological deformation optimizing vocal-motor output.
blocks.tts: History, anthropology and philology as retroactive data sciences. History shows the road we took, anthropology the maps we can draw, philology the language with which we name the world.
